transcript: An explainer video can reach people a slide deck misses, or it can shut them out. Here's how to make sure it brings more people in.
Text alone asks a lot of the reader. Video spreads the load across voice and image, and lets people pause, rewind and rewatch whenever they need.
But video isn't automatically accessible. Missing captions, low contrast, colour-only signals and rushed pacing all shut people out. Each one is fixable at the slide and script stage.
Say what the chart actually shows, so blind and low-vision viewers can follow too. Then caption everything, check contrast, and keep body text at 24 point or larger.
Swap a vague 'Results' headline and colour-coded pie for a clear statement and labelled bars. Now it works with sound or without, and with any colour vision.
On Pro, a.i. directs the video, timing gentle animation to your narration so viewers follow by ear and eye. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
